As the horizon extends to one week and then one month, the point estimates of 89.54 and 89.99, respectively, reflect an accumulation of these minor positive influences or a slight optimistic bias that is expected to materialize over the longer term, albeit still remaining very close to the initial value.

The widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the increasing uncertainty as we look further into the future. As we move to the 1-week horizon, the interval expands noticeably to [84.36, 94.72]. Conversely, significant negative events such as a sudden economic downturn, a major geopolitical shock, a severe supply chain disruption, or an unforeseen regulatory change could cause the outcome to drop below the 79.63 lower bound, particularly for the longer-term forecasts where such events have more time to manifest and impact the underlying conditions.
